dream: The tall palm pressed down on the tired wedge while the card hummed warm at fifty-one. I felt the heavy stump catch the slip, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waited in the quiet heat. The new corner felt light, as if it forgot its own thickness before I even pressed it down. The lid bit the air, sharp and thin, before slipping off entirely into the thin air where the stack was tired and the roof was flat. I pressed harder, pressing the turnip down on the stack, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move again.
